title: Seed synthetic usage so Console dashboards (cost/latency/errors) populate reliably in demo tenant
creator: Allison Grant
description:
Problem
- During live demos, Console dashboards (Usage, Cost, Latency, Error analysis, Rollouts views) frequently show empty graphs due to lack of recent traffic and/or missing seeded telemetry events. This undermines the “production economics” and “observability” segments and forces SEs into brittle manual workarounds.

Goal
- Provide a safe, synthetic, repeatable traffic + event seeding mechanism for the demo tenant so dashboards are always populated with realistic-looking data within minutes of a reset.
- Must not use any customer data. Must be clearly marked synthetic. Must be stable across model catalog changes via pinned demo routes.

Non-goals
- Perfect fidelity to every customer workload.
- Seeding historical data beyond what Console can reasonably ingest (we’ll target a rolling window rather than backfilling weeks).

Scope / What we need to generate
1) API traffic (primary)
- Chat completions: streaming + non-streaming
- Structured output route (JSON schema)
- Tool calling route (simulated tool invocation + follow-up)
- Embeddings + reranking (optional but preferred for Apex Retail-style narrative)

2) Telemetry distributions (make graphs look “real”)
- Request volume: steady baseline + gentle diurnal pattern; small burst windows to demonstrate autoscaling/rate-limit behavior without triggering 429s.
- Latency: distinct p50/p95/p99 curves; include a small tail of slower requests (e.g., longer prompts) to show breakdowns.
- Token usage: variable prompt/completion lengths; include longer-context requests at low frequency.
- Errors: low baseline error rate (e.g., 0.2–0.5%), plus a short controlled spike scenario for the error analysis view (toggleable).

3) Console-facing events
- Ensure events land in whatever pipelines power:
  - Cost breakdown by route/model
  - Latency charts and percentiles
  - Error codes / traces sampling (where enabled)
  - Rollout view (at least a canary/A-B “shape” with safe synthetic traffic)

Approach
- Implement a “synthetic traffic generator” job that runs in demo environments only.
- Traffic is generated by calling real Redwood API endpoints against the demo tenant using least-privilege keys.
- Configuration-driven presets (YAML/JSON) define:
  - routes to call (demo-pinned routes)
  - target RPS profile per route
  - prompt templates + parameter ranges
  - error injection policy (off by default; enabled only for a specific demo scenario)
  - region selection (default US; optional EU to support EMEA storyline)

Environment guards / safety
- Hard guard rails:
  - Require DEMO_TENANT=true (or equivalent) plus allowlist of org IDs.
  - Refuse to run against non-demo orgs even if credentials are valid.
  - Rate caps to avoid cost blowups.
- Synthetic marking:
  - Add a synthetic flag/tag to request metadata where supported (e.g., header or request attribute) so internal queries can segment demo traffic.

Acceptance criteria
- After a demo reset, within 5–10 minutes:
  - Usage/cost dashboards show non-empty charts in default time range.
  - Latency percentiles display plausible separation (p50 < p95 < p99).
  - Error analysis has at least some events, without overwhelming the narrative.
  - A rollout/A-B view can be shown with “traffic flowing” (even if it’s all synthetic).
- Job is idempotent and can run continuously (or on a schedule) without accumulating state.
- Runbook includes how to:
  - start/stop the generator
  - force a “warm dashboards now” run
  - enable the controlled error spike scenario

Open questions
- Where should the generator run?
  - Preferred: scheduled job in demo infra with explicit environment flags.
  - Alternate: SE-run CLI command that triggers a job (risk: forgetfulness).
- Do we need to write events directly into telemetry storage?
  - Preferred: call real APIs so the same ingestion path is exercised.

Implementation notes
- Coordinate with Logan Wright (Telemetry/analytics) on event tags and ensuring the default Console queries include demo traffic.
- Coordinate with Markus Klein on which routes are considered “known-good” and pinned.
- Coordinate with Sean Gallagher on safe rate caps + avoiding 429s during parallel demos.

Definition of Done
- Synthetic generator merged and deployed for demo environments.
- Demo tenant healthcheck includes a signal for “telemetry freshness” (last synthetic event timestamp).
- Reset runbook updated to include a deterministic step to repopulate dashboards.
- Dry-run validation: SE can run reset + warm dashboards and complete the observability segment without manual hacks.
comments:
2025-10-21 — Allison Grant (creator)
Creating as P0. We’re getting repeated field feedback that empty Console graphs are killing the observability + economics story. This needs to be automatic as part of the demo reset flow; SEs shouldn’t have to “click around until it fills in.”

2025-10-23 — Markus Klein
+1. Requirements from the demo script side: (1) cost breakdown by route must show multiple routes (chat, structured, tools), (2) latency chart must have a visible tail, (3) need a safe “error spike” we can toggle for the error analysis screen without risking a full demo outage.

2025-10-28 — Sean Gallagher
Please keep rate caps conservative and avoid any patterns that look like load testing. We’ve already seen 429s during demos. Also: parallel demos means this should work per-project namespace if possible (or at least not assume a single project is active).

2025-11-02 — Logan Wright
Telemetry note: if we tag synthetic traffic (header/attribute) we can both (a) filter internally and (b) ensure the default Console time range includes those events. Be careful not to accidentally exclude them in production queries; demo env only.

2025-11-08 — Mei Lin (assignee)
Draft plan: implement generator as a scheduled job that calls real API routes using scoped demo key. Config preset defines RPS + prompt templates. Will add hard org allowlist + DEMO_TENANT env guard. Target: dashboards non-empty within 10 min of reset.

2025-11-18 — Mei Lin
Implemented generator skeleton; early issue: embeddings endpoint emits different telemetry shape than chat; working with Logan to ensure Console aggregation handles it. Also adding a “warm run” mode (one-time burst for 3–5 minutes) used immediately after reset.

2025-12-01 — Allison Grant
QA feedback from dry run: graphs still empty if default Console time range is set to “Last 15 minutes” and generator hadn’t started yet. Please ensure reset flow triggers a warm run, not just relying on cron cadence.

2025-12-09 — Mei Lin
Addressed by adding a manual trigger endpoint/command path used by reset automation. Also added tiny error injection (HTTP 500 / timeout simulation) behind a flag; default OFF. Working on docs + runbook snippets.

2026-01-14 — Mei Lin
PR up: synthetic traffic generator job + config presets + environment allowlist. Includes tagging synthetic requests and a safe default cap. Requesting review from Logan (telemetry) + Sean (SRE) + Markus (demo flows).

2026-01-22 — Logan Wright
Reviewed. Tagging looks good. One change requested: ensure synthetic tag is recorded on both request + response events so cost and latency rollups align. Also: add a “last_event_ts” metric so healthcheck can detect ingestion stalls.

2026-02-03 — Sean Gallagher
Reviewed with minor nits: lower the burst rate during warm run to avoid tripping per-project quota in parallel demos; add jitter so traffic isn’t perfectly periodic (looks fake and can create batchy charts).

2026-02-12 — Mei Lin
Merged + deployed to demo env. Updated reset runbook to run warm dashboards step. Verified: after reset, Usage/Cost/Latency graphs populate within ~6 minutes; error analysis shows a few events; rollout view has continuous traffic. Marking Done.
